title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to the target.
You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
Return the answer in any order.
constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4

-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

-10^9 <= target <= 10^9

Exactly one valid answer exists.
hints: Can you avoid checking every possible pair?
Store previously seen numbers while traversing the array.
For each element x, check if target - x already exists.
companies: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Netflix, Accenture
editorialApproach:
Use a Hash Map to store previously visited numbers and their indices.
For every number:
1. Calculate complement = target - current number
2. Check whether complement already exists in hash map
3. If yes, return both indices
4. Otherwise store current number and index
editorialAlgorithm:
Initialize empty hash map

For each index i:

    complement = target - nums[i]

    If complement exists:
        return stored index and i

    Store nums[i] in map

Return result
